standard_prerequisites.name: An object of the first stage of the subcategory generated by an object is a direct summand of a finite direct sum of shifts of that object, and maps out of a shift of the ring into a complex are computed by the cohomology of the complex
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the case of one stage to the vanishing of a map whose induced map on cohomology is zero.

standard_prerequisites.name: An object of the n-th stage of the generated subcategory sits in a distinguished triangle whose first term is of the first stage and whose third term is of the previous stage
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides the induction step, after replacing the object by the object of the triangle.

standard_prerequisites.name: A morphism whose composite with the map to the third term of a distinguished triangle vanishes factors through that third term, by the representability statement for the homological functor
standard_prerequisites.use: Factors the first map of the chain and reduces the claim to the induction hypothesis applied to the remaining maps.

core_obligations: Treat the case of one stage: since the object is a direct summand of a finite direct sum of shifts of the ring and the maps out of such shifts are given by cohomology, the hypothesis that the maps are zero on cohomology makes any map out of the representing complex zero (proof lines 20679-20686).

For the induction, replace the object by the object of the distinguished triangle exhibiting the stage as an extension of an object of the first stage by an object of the previous stage, and note that it suffices to prove the vanishing for maps starting at that object (proof lines 20688-20700).

Use the case of one stage to see that the composite of the first map with the inclusion of the first stage vanishes, and apply the representability statement to factor the first map through the map to the third term of the triangle (proof lines 20701-20703).

Apply the induction hypothesis to the factored chain, whose maps are again zero on cohomology, to conclude that the composition of the remaining maps vanishes, and reassemble the original composition through the factorization to get the vanishing of the whole composition (proof lines 20704-20707).
proof_roadmap: One-stage case: decompose the object and use the cohomology description of maps out of shifts of the ring (proof lines 20679-20686).
Induction: use the distinguished triangle of the stage decomposition and factor the first map through the third term (proof lines 20688-20703).
Apply the induction hypothesis to the factored chain and reassemble (proof lines 20704-20707).
difficulty_reason: The statement is the ghost lemma: for an object of the n-th stage of the subcategory generated by the ring and a chain of n maps in the derived category, if every map in the chain is zero on cohomology then the composite vanishes (statement lines 20663-20677). The proof first settles the case of one stage by decomposing the object as a summand of shifts of the ring and using that maps out of a shift are computed by cohomology; the induction step then uses the distinguished triangle expressing a stage in terms of a one-stage object and the previous stage, factors the first map of the chain through the third term of the triangle using the one-stage case, and applies the induction hypothesis to the factored chain (proof lines 20679-20707). The factorization through the triangle is the heart of the induction.
